channel.title: Viktor Vidman
channel.description: Software architecture, AI-augmented delivery and local-first LLM infrastructure.

item.title: From Tier Map to Agent Team in GitHub Copilot
item.description: How to turn a model tier map into a model-independent agent team in GitHub Copilot: roles bound to tiers, tiers bound to models in one register, and where Copilot Fusion fits next to it.

item.title: The Model Register Is a Living Document
item.description: How to keep an organisation's AI model choices current: what a model register records, the five states a model moves through, two review rhythms, and how to handle a model that goes away.

item.title: Choosing Models Without an Eval Lab
item.description: How to choose the models for each tier when you have no internal evaluation lab: public benchmarks as a filter, five decision criteria, short trials and an eval library that grows out of real decisions.

item.title: Not Everyone Needs the Frontier Model
item.description: Why the models behind an organisation's AI coding assistants should be tiered by type of work, with one default and at most two alternatives per tier.

item.title: InferRouter Part 4: Observability
item.description: How InferRouter makes its internal state visible — a provider-agnostic JSONL operation log and three HTTP endpoints for live health, quota stats, and log history.

item.title: InferRouter Part 3: Secret Management
item.description: Where API keys live in InferRouter — why not environment variables, why not config files, and what per-request key reading gives you in practice.

item.title: InferRouter Part 2: Inference Strategies
item.description: How InferRouter decides which provider handles each request — three configurable inference strategies, the ProviderOrchestrator execution loop, and the local fallback that is always last.

item.title: InferRouter: One Endpoint, Any Provider
item.description: Why managing LLM providers per project breaks down — and how a single self-hosted proxy with strategy-based inference routing solves it.

item.title: Home Lab Docker Server and Deploy Workflow
item.description: How to turn an old machine or WSL2 into a personal Docker host, and set up a deploy workflow that works identically on both.

item.title: The Legacy BIOS + GPT Trap
item.description: Why older machines refuse to boot after a successful Linux installation, and how to fix it with Debian's classic installer.

item.title: Building the .NET AI Stack from First Principles
item.description: What I learned by wiring together LlamaSharp, Microsoft.Extensions.AI, and Semantic Kernel — and why the documentation does not tell the whole story.

item.title: From .NET Dev to AI Engineer — Why I Started This Series
item.description: I completed a strong theoretical course on Agentic AI. Then I realised I could not build anything with it. This is what I did about that.

item.title: VCS as Proof Store
item.description: Why duplicate source content into a proof database when source control already tracks everything? SourceRAG uses the VCS itself as its proof store — no content duplication, full traceability.

item.title: Making a 2M-line legacy codebase queryable by AI
item.description: I designed a system to make a 2M+ line on-premise legacy codebase queryable by any AI tool. It was presented, never implemented. Here is the design — and the question it left open.

item.title: Building a RAG Pipeline from Scratch
item.description: What I learned by building a RAG pipeline in .NET without a framework — every component written from scratch, every decision made consciously.

item.title: Closing the Loop
item.description: A practical workflow for pairing a reasoning model with an agentic coding assistant — and closing the structural gap between planning and implementation.

item.title: ChaosForge - Let Go of the Reins
item.description: From Scaffold Protocol to ChaosForge – why I stopped trying to control every AI step, and what I built instead.

item.title: The AI Executes. You Decide.
item.description: How Scaffold Protocol keeps the human as orchestrator while using AI as a transformation engine — with a real validation layer and error-driven refinement.

item.title: The generator pipeline — from Markdown to GitHub Pages
item.description: No CI/CD. No build server. A local command, a docs/ folder, and a git push. Here's the full picture.

item.title: Designing a minimal DSL for bilingual Markdown content
item.description: One file. Two languages. No duplication. Here's the syntax that makes it work.
